name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 partisan lean of the district
Incumbent Ronny Jackson with $5.4M cash on hand vs. $14K for Nair
No polling and no expert ratings; markets price ~4% for Democrats
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Jackson's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and Polymarket pricing Democrats at roughly 4% all point the same direction, with no polling or ratings offering any reason to move. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin of about R+20.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement could open the door, but nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ronny Jackson seeks reelection in one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, a Texas Panhandle seat with a R+23 partisan lean. He enters the general election with a huge financial edge, having raised over $4 million and holding $5.4 million on hand, plus modest outside support. Challenger Mark Nair has raised about $102,000 with little cash remaining.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. With no evidence pointing toward a competitive race, the seat is rated Safe Republican, with the expected margin near twenty points in Jackson's favor.
